text:
janet: FYI Acme (customer) is seeing 5xx/403 spikes and >600ms p99 today. They say traffic from their VPC (eu-west) is landing on our us-west pool. Logs show X-Forwarded-Region: us-west. Repro steps from them: curl -> our /v1/generate returns 403 sometimes and a 200 with ~700ms latency other times. sample curl they sent:
```curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Host: api.redwood.example'```
They suspect VPC egress NAT or peering causing wrong-region egress. Opening thread so eng/network can triage.

ops-bot: Alert: customer-acme high-error-rate (rate 12% over 5m) — routed to support channel. SLA impact: possible. :warning: 

sasha: @janet thanks. Can you ask them to paste the TCP src ip we see in our logs (x-client-ip) and a traceroute from one of their app nodes? Also ask them to curl with `-H "X-Forwarded-For: <their-ip>" -v` so we can compare headers. Quick checklist: preserved source IP? proxy-protocol? any egress NAT appliance?

acme-ops: janet here's the traceroute and one app node curl output. traceroute -> shows first hop to our peering peer in us-west. curl -v shows:
* Connected to api.redwood.example (3.120.45.77) port 443
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< x-region: us-west
We do have an on-prem NAT appliance that hairpins into our VPC peering. Routes configured to prefer path to us-west (we thought eu-west).

mike: Thanks @acme-ops. Likely SNAT hole: their NAT appliance rewrites src to a shared pool that announces via a us-west egress. Two quick checks on our side: 1) which region received their source IP (we map src ip -> region via ip->peering table) 2) examine BGP next-hop for that prefix. I pulled a bgp/peers dump and see the /24 for 3.120.45.0/24 is learned via us-west session.
```bgp> show route 3.120.45.0/24
-> 3.120.45.0/24 via 192.0.2.1 (us-west peer) [localpref 100]
```
If their NAT pool is owned by Acme but announced from us-west, traffic will terminate in us-west by design.

sasha: Two mitigation paths: (A) ask Acme to preserve source (disable SNAT) or use 1:1 NAT so the prefix is announced from eu-west; (B) we can add a routing override to prefer eu-west for that customer id (short-term) — but note this can break if that prefix truly is only reachable via us-west. Also can accept `X-Client-Region` header from their egress if they control the proxy and we validate TLs.

acme-ops: We control the appliance but we can't disable SNAT globally right now. We can do 1:1 NAT for a small set of IPs. Happy to do that for a test pair. Also curious if there's something we can change on Redwood side (route preference) while we test.

mike: If they can 1:1 NAT two IPs we can update our route-map to prefer eu-west for those exact IPs (more specific /32s). That avoids mass route overrides. Steps: Acme gives two public IPs -> we accept routes from their ASN via peering -> we pin route preference to eu-west for those prefixes. I'll prepare a canary change and a rollback plan.

sasha: Good. Also recording repro steps for docs: 1) customer egress SNAT -> announces shared NAT prefix from different region -> our smart-routing routes to advertised region -> customer sees wrong-region. 2) temporary fixes: 1:1 NAT, advertise /32s from correct region, or client-side header + trust config for private deployments. Long term: improve region-fallback to consider customer-configured home-region metadata before BGP/peering route.

janet: I'll schedule a call with Acme + mike + sasha tomorrow 9am CET to coordinate 1:1 NAT test. Acme, please confirm two test IPs and sample curl when ready.

acme-ops: Confirmed — we'll allocate 198.51.100.9 and 198.51.100.10 and will announce them from eu-west once you say go. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

mike: I'll stage the route-map change in our staging router and post the config diff in this thread before making production changes.

sasha: Marking as customer-impacting and adding to Monday runbook. If we see more customers with similar setups we should make a playbook: check source ASN/prefix advertisement -> ask for 1:1 or accept forwarded region header -> route override canary.

ops-bot: Incident tracker updated (INC-2026-0453) — assigned to mike/sasha.

janet: thanks everyone. I'll update Acme with meeting invite and next steps.
